gemini.rationale: The transaction was a holding company collapse where HRG acquired the remaining minority interest in Spectrum. The operating business (T4, T5) and organization (T6) of Spectrum transferred intact (1-1) into the surviving structure, with no structural mismatch documented at closing. The controlling stockholder (HRG's control block) was eliminated, resulting in a termination of the prior controlling intent.

grok.rationale: At closing the First Merger left Spectrum as surviving wholly owned subsidiary with its customer products and operating processes intact inside that same entity; the separate GBA divestiture was expressly outside the Merger terms and had not closed. Spectrum’s pre-merger officers became the officers of the renamed parent and six of seven post-close directors were then-current Spectrum directors, so T5 and T6 moved together with no contractual TSA needed to bridge a mismatch. Consequently neither a product-vs-process nor a process-vs-organization structural gap existed at closing.

openai.rationale: The structural summary states that the pre-merger operating company survived as a wholly owned subsidiary and that the separate batteries/appliances divestiture proceeded alongside, rather than as part of, the merger; nothing documents products crossing without their associated operations, so gap_45 is 0. The slice also states that Spectrum's pre-merger board and executive officers were carried forward as the renamed parent's governance and management, documenting coherent alignment of operations and organization at closing; therefore gap_56 is 0.
